key_insight: Surface orientation in low-dimensional pnictogen chalcohalides can shift band edges by up to 0.8 eV, making facet control a critical lever for charge extraction and photovoltaic performance.
engineering_relevance: The work shows that selecting or engineering stable surface facets such as (011) and (010) could materially improve contact alignment and open-circuit voltage in MChX solar cells.
method: First-principles calculations across the full MChX family
Exhaustive crystal-orientation sampling, including low-symmetry facets
evidence_signal: The study finds that the most stable (011) and (010) surfaces differ in formation energy by only about 0.01–0.03 J m^-2, yet their band edges can shift by up to 0.8 eV and reduce Voc by as much as 0.6 V in simulation.
watch_item: The results are based on idealized, defect-free models, so real devices may show additional effects from defects, roughness, and mixed facet distributions.
paper_title: Surface Physics of Low-Dimensional Pnictogen Chalcohalides and Its Impact on Photovoltaic Technologies
